newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on good news to be short-lived.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on good news to be short-lived.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Friday in early trade and dealers attributed the growth to better Russian buying on good corporate news and occasional foreign orders.
But they forecast the rise would be short-lived.
Traders said they saw most interest in national power utility UES, partly due to its forthcoming American Depositary Receipts issue.

"The UES news spurred mostly Russian buying, while clients are picking up small packages of the shares which look most attractive," said United City Bank chief trader Samit Yakovlev. "There appeared some clients' support, but it is just a small occasional interest to traditional papers."
A UES official said on Thursday the company plans to issue level-one ADRs in two or three months.
Yakovlev said foreign buying in UES was only due to the ADR news.
"In my view such buying on good news cannot support price growth for a long time," he said.
At 0920 GMT UES rose to $0.2225 from $0.2105 at Thursday's close.

Head of securities department at Bank Rossiisky Kredit Oleg Martynenko said the interest to UES, Moscow power utility Mosenergo and LUKoil was mostly due to portfolio and temporary interest rather than to any news.

"People are just trying to build up their portfolios before the long holidays and look at traditionally good papers, which you can buy at a good price," he said. "It is like a game -- to buy now at a good price and to wait until the holidays are over."
Russian markets are most likely to be closed May 1-4 and May 9-11, but there has not yet been any official announcement about market holidays. May 1 and May 9 are public holidays.
Mosenergo rose to $1.258 from $1.235 and LUKoil was up to $13.50 after $13.40.
LUKoil said on Friday its $200 million convertible bond issue last week was oversubscribed.
It also said it expects to issue level-three ADRs in the first quarter of 1998.
Traders forecast a calm market before the holidays.
"I do not think something significant will happen today and especially next short week due to the forthcoming holidays," Martynenko said.
